Subject: New Step Before Starting a PIP — What's Changing and Why

Hi everyone,

We want to share an update to how we handle performance improvement plans, along with the reasoning behind it.

Over the past year, we've seen real inconsistency in how PIPs have been initiated across teams. In some cases, employees have entered a formal PIP process without a clear prior record of the concerns being raised with them — which isn't fair to the employee, and has created situations where we couldn't fully reconstruct what happened or when. That's a problem we want to fix, both because employees deserve a documented trail of feedback before things escalate formally, and because we as an organization need to be able to stand behind our process if it's ever questioned.

**What's changing:**

Starting **February 3, 2025**, managers will be required to complete a brief performance concern documentation form before initiating any PIP. This documentation should capture:

- The specific performance or behavior concern
- When it was first observed
- What conversations or feedback have already taken place
- What support or resources were offered

This isn't a new bureaucratic hurdle — it's a step that should already reflect conversations you've been having. If you're at the point of considering a PIP and you can't fill this out, that's a signal the employee may need more coaching time before formal action is appropriate.

The form will be available in Workday starting **January 27, 2025**, giving you a week to review it before the requirement takes effect. HR Business Partners will also hold a walkthrough session on **January 29, 2025** — calendar invite coming separately.

If you have questions about how this works in practice — especially for situations already in progress — please reach out to **Dani Okafor** directly. You can message Dani on Slack at **@daniokafor** or email **d.okafor@[company].com**. Dani is also holding open office hours on **January 28, 2025 from 2–4 PM** for anyone who wants to talk through a specific situation before the deadline.

We know this adds a step to an already difficult process. We're making this change because we want the process to be one we can all trust — managers, employees, and the organization alike.

Thanks for everything you do to support your teams.

[Sender name]

Subject: New Step Before Starting a PIP — What's Changing and Why

Hi everyone,

Here's something we've been seeing that isn't working well: employees entering a formal PIP process without a clear prior record of the concerns being raised with them. No documented feedback. No paper trail of the coaching conversations that should have happened first. That's not fair to the employee — and it means we can't fully reconstruct what happened or when, which puts everyone in a difficult position.

This has been inconsistent across teams, and we want to fix it.

**What's changing:**

Starting **February 3, 2025**, managers will be required to complete a brief performance concern documentation form before initiating any PIP. This documentation should capture:

- The specific performance or behavior concern
- When it was first observed
- What conversations or feedback have already taken place
- What support or resources were offered

This isn't a new bureaucratic hurdle — it's a step that should already reflect conversations you've been having. If you're at the point of considering a PIP and you can't fill this out, that's a signal the employee may need more coaching time before formal action is appropriate.

The form will be available in Workday starting **January 27, 2025**. The requirement takes effect **February 3, 2025**, giving you one week to review the form and ask questions before it becomes mandatory. We are also holding a walkthrough session on **January 29, 2025** — calendar invite coming separately.

If you have questions about how this works in practice — especially for situations already in progress — please reach out to **Dani Okafor** directly. You can message Dani on Slack at **@daniokafor** or email **d.okafor@[company].com**. Dani is also holding open office hours on **January 28, 2025 from 2–4 PM** for anyone who wants to talk through a specific situation before the deadline.

We know this adds a step to an already difficult process. We are making this change because we want the process to be one we can all trust — managers, employees, and the organization alike.

Thanks for everything you do to support your teams.

[Sender name]
